status.description:
Payment status.
    `paid`: payment collected in full.
    `partially_paid`: some amount collected, but a balance remains.
    `refunded`: full refund issued. `amountPaid` still shows the original amount, not the net amount after refund. Use `amountRefunded` for the refund amount and `lastRefundAt` for the refund date.
    `partial_refund`: partial refund issued. Use `amountRefunded` for the refund amount and `amountPaid - amountRefunded` for the net amount retained. `lastRefundAt`, `lastRefundReason`, and `lastRefundReasonNote` describe the most recent refund action.
    `draft`: checkout in progress and not yet submitted.
    `draft_expired`: checkout started but expired before completion.
    `created`: payment record created, but no action taken yet.
    `pending`: payment submitted and awaiting processing.
    `unpaid`: manual or invoice payment created, but not yet paid. This is expected for invoice-based checkouts and is not a failure state.
    `failed`: payment attempt was rejected. Check `paymentError` for the most recent error message when present.
    `canceled`: payment was canceled.

availabilityBehavior.description:
Controls when the ticket becomes available for purchase.

| Value | Description | Required fields |
|-------|-------------|-----------------|
| `always_available` | Always on sale (default). | — |
| `date_time_based` | On sale between `saleStartOn` and `saleEndOn`. Omit either date to leave that end open. | `saleStartOn` and/or `saleEndOn` |
| `after_ticket_sale_ends` | Becomes available once the trigger ticket's `saleEndOn` is reached. Useful for sequential sale windows (e.g. Early Bird → Standard). | `triggerTicketType` or `triggerTicketGroup` |
| `after_ticket_sold_out` | Becomes available once the trigger ticket sells out. | `triggerTicketType` or `triggerTicketGroup` |
| `after_ticket_ends_or_sold_out` | Becomes available once the trigger ticket's sale ends **or** it sells out, whichever comes first. | `triggerTicketType` or `triggerTicketGroup` |
| `until_event_starts` | On sale until the event's `startDate` is reached. | — |

PagePaymentOptionInput.description:
Configures a single payment option shown at checkout. Only these enabled combinations are supported: `full`, `invoice`, `partial`, `cash_on_delivery`, `full + invoice`, `full + partial`, or `full + cash_on_delivery`. Multiple options can be combined (e.g. pay in full + pay via invoice) or a single option can be offered alone.

**Option types:**
- `full` — customer pays the entire amount immediately.
- `manual` — no payment is collected at checkout. A confirmation with an invoice is sent and the order is marked unpaid. Set `manualType` to `invoice` or `cash_on_delivery`.
- `partial` — customer pays `partialAmount` now; the remaining balance is due later and the order is marked as partially paid.

Digital files and event tickets are always issued immediately after checkout regardless of which option the customer selects. [Learn more](https://checkoutpage.com/docs/articles/manual-payments-pay-in-full-by-invoice-pay-deposit-or-cash-on-delivery)

ProductDetailsInput.description:
Product configuration for checkout pages.

Use this object to define pricing mode, subscription/payment plan behavior, inventory, variants, and conditional variant visibility.

Common setup patterns:
- Standard one-time checkout: set `price.amount` and `price.currency`.
- Variant-driven pricing: set `price.amount` to `0` (or omit it) and define `variants` with per-option `additionalChargeAmount`.
- Subscriptions (recurring): configure `price.recurring`.
- Payment plans (fixed installments): configure `price.paymentPlan` with `planIterations`.
- Multiple selectable prices: use `prices[]`; `price` is the single-price alias and `pricingType` is deprecated (accepted and ignored).

Important rules:
- You cannot set both `price.recurring` and `price.paymentPlan`.
- `price.payWhatYouWant` applies to one-time prices and subscriptions, but not payment plans.
- When both `trialPeriodDays` and `startDate` are set, `startDate` wins.
- For conditional variant logic (`showHideLogic`) or `preselect`, set a `key` on variants/options to enable cross-references. Keys are not persisted.

discounts.description:
Bulk discounts applied when a customer purchases a minimum quantity. Two modes are supported:

**`checkout_quantity`** — discount applies based on the total checkout quantity, regardless of which variant options are selected.

**`variant_option_quantity`** — discount applies only when specific variant options meet the quantity threshold. To use this mode you must link the discount to variant options using temporary `key` values: assign a `key` to each relevant option in `variants[].options[].key`, then reference those same keys in `variantOptionIds[].key` within the same request. These keys are resolved to MongoDB ObjectIds at save time and are not present in the response — so the linking must be established in the same request that defines (or redefines) the variants. You cannot attach a `variant_option_quantity` discount to an existing product's variant options without also re-supplying the `variants` array with keys in the same PATCH request.

[Learn more](https://checkoutpage.com/docs/articles/bulk-discounts)

variantOptionIds.description: Variant options this discount applies to. Each entry must reference a variant option by the `key` you assigned to it in `variants[].options[].key` within the same request. Option keys are temporary caller-defined handles — they are resolved to MongoDB ObjectIds at save time and do not appear in the response. Only used when `quantityCondition` is `variant_option_quantity`.

discounts.description:
Bulk discounts applied when a customer purchases a minimum quantity. Two modes are supported:

**`checkout_quantity`** — discount applies based on the total checkout quantity, regardless of which variant options are selected.

**`variant_option_quantity`** — discount applies only when specific variant options meet the quantity threshold. To use this mode you must link the discount to variant options using temporary `key` values: assign a `key` to each relevant option in `variants[].options[].key`, then reference those same keys in `variantOptionIds[].key` within the same request. These keys are resolved to MongoDB ObjectIds at save time and are not present in the response — so the linking must be established in the same request that defines (or redefines) the variants. You cannot attach a `variant_option_quantity` discount to an existing product's variant options without also re-supplying the `variants` array with keys in the same PATCH request.

[Learn more](https://checkoutpage.com/docs/articles/bulk-discounts)

Each entry must reference a variant option by the `key` you assigned to it in `variants[].options[].key` within the same request. post.description:
Creates a checkout page together with its product and default fields in a single request.

Use this endpoint whenever you need to accept payments. It supports four payment flows, controlled by the `productData.price` object:

- **One-time payment** — set `price.amount` and `price.currency`. Do not set `price.recurring`, `price.paymentPlan`, or `price.payWhatYouWant`.
- **Pay What You Want (PWYW)** — set `price.payWhatYouWant: true`. `price.amount` becomes the minimum; leave it at `0` to allow free purchases. PWYW cannot be combined with subscriptions or payment plans.
- **Subscription (recurring)** — set `price.recurring` with `interval` (`day`, `week`, `month`, or `year`) and `intervalCount`. Optionally add `trialPeriodDays` or a `billingCycleAnchorConfig`.
- **Payment plan (installments)** — set `price.paymentPlan` with `interval`, `intervalCount`, and `planIterations` (the fixed number of payments after which the plan completes).

`price.recurring` and `price.paymentPlan` are mutually exclusive — set only one.

Default name and email fields are always created automatically. Pass `fields` to add extra checkout fields.

post.description: Triggered when a ticket is created for an event booking

ticket.description: A single admission ticket held by one attendee, created when an event booking is paid. Read-only.

allOf.description: Id of the booking (Charge) this ticket was created from. A booking of three tickets produces three ticket records sharing one `bookingId`. Retrieve it with the bookings endpoint.

canceledAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the ticket was canceled. Absent while the ticket is valid.

allOf.description: Deprecated alias of `bookingId`. Use `bookingId` instead.

checkIns.description: Full check-in history, oldest first. Empty when the guest has never been checked in. A guest checked in and back out again has multiple entries.

checkedInAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the check-in was recorded.

allOf.description: Id of the user (event staff or seller) who performed the check-in.

method.description: How the check-in happened. `QRSCAN` is the ticket QR code scanned at the door, `MANUAL` is door staff tapping the check-in button.

status.description: Check-in state recorded by this scan. `CHECKEDIN` admitted the guest, `UNCHECKEDIN` reversed an earlier check-in.

couponAmount.description: Coupon discount allocated to this ticket, in the smallest currency unit. Booking-level coupon discounts are apportioned across the tickets in the booking.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the ticket record was created.

currency.description: Lowercase ISO 4217 currency code for every amount on the ticket (e.g. "usd").

allOf.description: Deprecated alias of `customerId`. Use `customerId` instead.

customerEmail.description: Email of the customer who booked, denormalised at purchase time. The ticket is delivered here.

allOf.description: Id of the customer who booked the ticket.

customerName.description: Name of the customer who booked, denormalised at purchase time.

discountAmount.description: Bulk discount allocated to this ticket, in the smallest currency unit. Booking-level discounts are apportioned across the tickets in the booking.

feeAmount.description: Booking fees allocated to this ticket, in the smallest currency unit. Booking-level fees are apportioned across the tickets in the booking.

latestCheckIn.description: Most recent entry from `checkIns`, denormalised for filtering. Absent when the guest has never been checked in — treat that as not checked in.

checkedInAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the check-in was recorded.

allOf.description: Id of the user (event staff or seller) who performed the check-in.

method.description: How the check-in happened. `QRSCAN` is the ticket QR code scanned at the door, `MANUAL` is door staff tapping the check-in button.

status.description: Check-in state recorded by this scan. `CHECKEDIN` admitted the guest, `UNCHECKEDIN` reversed an earlier check-in.

livemode.description: Whether the ticket came from a live payment. Test-mode tickets are never returned by the seller API.

metadata.description: Custom key/value entries attached to the ticket, typically written by door staff during check-in. Maximum 20 entries.

addedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the entry was added.

value.description: Metadata value. Maximum 100 characters.

orderId.description: Human-readable order reference shared by every ticket in the same booking. Shown to the customer on receipts and tickets.

orderedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the booking was placed. Matches across every ticket in the same booking.

originalPrice.description: Price of the ticket before any discounts, coupons, taxes or fees, in the smallest currency unit (e.g. cents).

allOf.description: Deprecated alias of `pageId`. Use `pageId` instead.
Id of the event page the ticket was purchased from.

pricing.description: Pricing model of the ticket type at the time of purchase. `paid` is a fixed price, `pwyw` means the buyer chose the amount, `free` is a zero-price ticket. Absent on tickets created before this field existed.

revenue.description: Revenue attributed to this ticket, in the smallest currency unit: `originalPrice - discountAmount - couponAmount + taxAmount + feeAmount`. Use this rather than summing the parts yourself.

allOf.description: Deprecated alias of `sellerId`. Use `sellerId` instead.
Id of the seller account the ticket belongs to.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the ticket. `PAID` is valid for admission, `CANCELED` was voided by refund or cancellation and must not be admitted.

taxAmount.description: Tax allocated to this ticket, in the smallest currency unit. Booking-level tax is apportioned across the tickets in the booking.

ticketShortId.description: Short uppercase alphanumeric code identifying the ticket (e.g. "A1B2C3D4"). Printed on the ticket and quoted by guests at the door — search on it to find a specific attendee.

allOf.description: Deprecated alias of `ticketTypeId`. Use `ticketTypeId` instead.
Id of the ticket type purchased (e.g. General Admission, VIP). Ticket types belong to a ticket group on the event.

updatedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the ticket record was last updated.

allOf.description: Unique identifier. Must be in BSON ObjectId format.
Unique identifier. Must be in BSON ObjectId format.
